item.title: Optimizations of the ATLAS ITk GNN reconstruction pipeline
item.description: We present refinements and optimizations of the Graph Neural Network (GNN) tracking pipeline for the ATLAS Inner Tracker, including updated physics performance, robustness against detector defects, and computational improvements such as model compression and structured pruning.

item.title: Computational Performance of the ATLAS ITk GNN Track Reconstruction Pipeline
item.description: We describe a variety of improvements to the algorithmic implementations and machine learning models of the GNN-based track reconstruction pipeline for the ATLAS ITk, significantly decreasing execution times from minutes to hundreds of milliseconds.

item.title: Physics Performance of the ATLAS GNN4ITk Track Reconstruction Chain
item.description: This paper presents an algorithm based on Graph Neural Network for charged-particle track reconstruction in the ATLAS Inner Tracker. Using realistic simulation data, we demonstrate the performance of the algorithm in comparison with the state-of-the-art technique.

item.title: Simulation of Hadronic Interactions with Deep Generative Models
item.description: We explore the use of conditional normalizing flow in the simulation of interaction between hadronic particles and atomic nuclei in ordinary matter. We trained generative models to reproduce data simulated by the state-of-the-art simulator, conditioned on the kinematics of the incoming hadron.

item.title: A Language Model for Particle Tracking
item.description: We present a tokenized detector representation that allows training a BERT model (TrackingBERT) for particle tracking. This work represents a first step towards a foundational model for particle detector understanding.

item.title: Hierarchical Graph Neural Networks for Particle Track Reconstruction
item.description: We introduce a novel variant of GNN for particle tracking called Hierarchical Graph Neural Network (HGNN), together with a learnable pooling algorithm (GMPool) and a dedicated loss function, showing improved tracking efficiency and robustness over traditional GNNs.
